findings: ghd_02_19.tex:843, 'It is immediate that ... V is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy hypersurface S': it relies on the ambient U₁ (ghd_02_19.tex:841, 'we require W_p ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂'). The pieces S_p give every inextensible curve of V a meeting with S, through its component in one DS_p. That the meeting is unique needs S acausal (or Cauchy) in U₁ ⊇ V. GH then follows, in ERS's Lorentzian setting from the Cauchy property (Geroch), so U₁ is used once, for the uniqueness of the meeting. In ETT, without Geroch (iii) ⇒ (i), GH comes from causal convexity of V in the GH U₁ (IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn). Without an ambient, local developments of pieces of S can union to a set of which S is not a Cauchy surface (Causal.timelikeLine_not_isCauchySurfaceOn_union). That example is in 1+0 dimensions with S = {0, 1} disconnected, whereas ERS's S is connected (:814). No error; the dependence is unstated.
The proof never uses that u₂ is a GHD except through Sogge's local uniqueness, and never uses the connectedness of S assumed at :812, :814.

Reading taken: this is the PDE input. It is not a predicate on one causality, so it cannot be a ladder node of sort causality.

OQ-57 (c) reads common developments with 'S Cauchy, GH not concluded'. Here GH of V is proved for every common development inside a GH U₁ that is causally arc-connected with curves extending (IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn; also V₀ of Thm 4.64 and Remark 4.67's U₁ ∩ U₂, ers_remark_4_67_globallyHyperbolicOn). No Geroch (iii) ⇒ (i) is involved. This is evidence for OQ-57 (c), not a ruling. Reading kept: IsCommonDevelopment unchanged (S Cauchy), GH stated as a separate conclusion.

findings: ghd_02_19.tex:1021, 'Hence, we can finish the proof by constructing a GHD u : U → R ... by setting U = ⋃_{p∈S} DS_p': the Cauchy property and the global hyperbolicity of U are asserted without argument. They do not follow from local developments alone: Causal.timelikeLine_not_isCauchySurfaceOn_union gives local developments of pieces of S whose union does not have S as Cauchy surface (1+0 dimensions, S disconnected). A connected 2+1 analogue would use the winding hypersurface of ghd_02_19.tex:930 (not formalised). It lies outside ERS's construction, which the flow tube T excludes: W_p ⊆ T, the image of the flow Φ of N (:1011), with N timelike on DS_p. By ERS's own argument at :1014, the integral curve through a point of DS_p ∩ DS_q meets S once, in S_p ∩ S_q, so local developments on adjacent sheets cannot overlap. This is not a failure of ERS's construction. What does give the Cauchy property is the claim's by-product: S is Cauchy in each DS_p ∩ DS_q, because D_pS_A ∩ D_qS_A = A on every component. With that, Theorem 4.77's open-closed argument applies (ghd_02_19.tex:1037-1044, given only later). It is formalised as Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_inf, with the causality of U, itself a part of the printed conclusion, assumed. GH of U is Geroch (iii) ⇒ (i) and is not concluded.

ghd_02_19.tex:1014-1021: the component step (Theorem 4.64 on D_pS_A, D_qS_A, then the boundary argument with (4.76)) can be replaced by Theorem 4.64's own argument run inside the component A (Causal.Causality.maxDevelopmentIn_eq). This needs no domain of dependence and no 'a posteriori' connectedness of A ∩ S_p ∩ S_q (:1014). The boundary argument itself, in particular ':1021, The global hyperbolicity of DS_p and DS_q shows that γ has to intersect S_p ∩ S_q', was bypassed and not audited.
questions: Reading of the causalities: each local solution has its own causality cau i (of g(u_i)), in which its development and the component restart are read. The patched causality Cu is any causality that agrees with every cau i on the open subsets of D i and whose ≤_U is antisymmetric; it is quantified after v is constructed, so its supplier, g(v), is not circular. Is this the formalisation of record? The fixed-background reading is the instance cau i = Cu = C.

Reading of the claim: ERS's 4.64 on the domains of dependence D_pS_A, D_qS_A plus the boundary argument is replaced by 4.64's argument in the component A. Its named inputs (RestartsIn) are 4.64's, located in A: 'A meets S' (from N); Prop 4.63's local uniqueness on S ∩ A and SliceRestart in A (supplier T-loc-quasilinear-slice); FrontierStaysIn in A (supplier T-loc-quasilinear-frontier). Both T-loc targets are scoped today to W = U₁, L = U₁ ∩ U₂ and common developments, while RestartsIn asks W = DS_p, L a component of DS_p ∩ DS_q and IsDevelopmentIn. The component-located forms are a scope question for both targets, for the planner. Reading taken: the same layer-3 arguments apply; for FrontierStaysIn, the null generator stays in DS_q by 4.64's argument, and so in the component by connectedness.

The causality of U for Cu (hcaus) is a part of the printed conclusion (U a GHD, :1021) assumed: accept as in ers_theorem_4_77 (OQ-41 (d)), or should it be supplied? For a general quasilinear equation no T-loc target supplies it (T-loc-quasilinear-nesting's is_causal needs (4.62)).

kb_proposals: kb entry (pattern) 'Unions of local developments of pieces of S': opens D with Cauchy surfaces S' ⊆ S, inside an ambient B. If S is acausal in B and ≤_B antisymmetric, then S is a Cauchy surface of ⋃ D (Causal.Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_sSup_of_isAcausalOn). The same holds with S Cauchy in B and CurvesExtendOn B (…_of_curvesExtendOn). If moreover B is GH and causally arc-connected and S ⊆ ⋃ D, then ⋃ D is causally convex in B and GH (globallyHyperbolicOn_sSup_of_pieces). Without the ambient this fails (timelikeLine_not_isCauchySurfaceOn_union). A common development inside a GH, arc-connected, curves-extending U₁ is GH with no Geroch (IsCommonDevelopment.globallyHyperbolicOn) (T-abs-ers-unions).

kb entry (pattern) 'Theorem 4.64 in a region': IsDevelopmentIn S L agree V (V ≤ L, S ∩ L ⊆ V, agree, S Cauchy in V) and maxDevelopmentIn_eq / ers_theorem_4_64_in run ERS's Steps 1, 2 and the restart in any preconnected open L ≤ W that meets S, with local uniqueness on S ∩ L. Use it for components of overlaps (Thm 4.75) instead of domains of dependence. IsCommonDevelopment is the case L = U₁ ⊓ U₂ ⊇ S (isCommonDevelopment_iff_isDevelopmentIn) (T-abs-ers-unions).

kb note (pitfall) 'ers_theorem_4_77 does not need S ⊆ Uᵢ': the union argument holds with S Cauchy in each Uᵢ and Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ only (isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_inf). A Cauchy surface of every component (Causal.componentOpens, connectedComponentIn of an open as Opens, M locally connected) is a Cauchy surface of the open set (isCauchySurfaceOn_of_componentOpens). For S = {s}, GH gives the compact slabs (GloballyHyperbolicOn.compactSlabs_singleton) (T-abs-ers-unions).
